items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I have a cat named Stripe. I feed her every morning.

Does this story use the word 'I'? Yes or no?

steps: The story says 'I have a cat' and 'I feed her.' The word 'I' appears twice.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I have a cat named Stripe. I feed her every morning.

Is the narrator first-person or third-person?

steps: The narrator uses 'I,' which means they are telling their own story. That is first-person.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Leo has a cat named Stripe. He feeds her every morning.

Is the narrator first-person or third-person?

steps: The narrator uses 'Leo' and 'He,' not 'I.' Someone outside the story is telling it. That is third-person.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Maya picked up her backpack. She walked to school.

Which word tells you the narrator is third-person?

steps: The narrator uses 'Maya' and 'She' to talk about the character. These words show the narrator is outside the story.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I ran to the door. I opened it. My dog ran in.

Who is telling this story: the narrator or a character named Maya?

steps: The narrator uses 'I' and 'My.' We do not know their name, but they are telling their own story. It is a first-person narrator.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Sam looked at the sky. 'It is going to rain,' he said.

Who says 'It is going to rain'?

steps: The words 'It is going to rain' are in quotation marks. The sentence says 'he said' and the character is Sam. So Sam is speaking.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Aisha looked at her friend. 'Want to play?' she asked.

How do you know Aisha is speaking?
items.answer: Her words are inside quotation marks and the text says 'she asked.'

steps: Quotation marks show when a character is speaking. 'She asked' tells us Aisha is the one asking the question.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Ben looked at the big slide. 'I am going to go down it,' he said.

In the sentence inside the quotation marks, who is 'I'?

steps: The quotation marks show Ben is speaking. Inside the quote, he uses 'I' to mean himself. So 'I' refers to Ben.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I love pizza more than anything. My favorite topping is cheese.

Circle the word that tells you this is a first-person narrator: (I / She / Marco)

steps: The word 'I' in 'I love pizza' is the clue. A first-person narrator uses 'I' to tell their own story.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Zoe ran to the window. She watched the snow fall.

Circle the word that tells you this is a third-person narrator: (I / She / My)

steps: The word 'She' refers to Zoe, and it is used by someone outside the story. That is a third-person narrator.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

'What time is it?' asked Marco. 'It is three o'clock,' said his mom.

How many characters speak in this passage?
items.answer: Two characters: Marco and his mom.

steps: Marco speaks: 'What time is it?' His mom speaks: 'It is three o'clock.' Two characters speak.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

I got a new book today. I read it all before dinner. I loved it.

Who is telling this story?

steps: The word 'I' is used three times. The narrator is telling their own story. This is a first-person narrator.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Leo saw a bug on his desk. He picked it up carefully and put it outside.

Who is telling this story: Leo or someone else?

steps: The narrator uses 'Leo' and 'He' to talk about Leo. The narrator is not Leo. Someone outside the story is telling it.

items.prompt: True or false: In a first-person story, the narrator uses words like 'he' and 'she' to talk about themselves.

steps: In a first-person story, the narrator uses 'I' to talk about themselves. 'He' and 'she' are used by a third-person narrator talking about other characters.

items.prompt:
Read this story below.

Aisha looked at her sister. 'Can I have some?' she asked. Her sister smiled. 'Yes,' she said. 'Take as much as you want.'

How many characters speak? Write their words.
items.answer: Two characters speak. Aisha says: 'Can I have some?' Her sister says: 'Yes. Take as much as you want.'

steps: Aisha speaks first: 'Can I have some?' Then her sister speaks: 'Yes. Take as much as you want.' Two characters speak, and their words are in quotation marks.
